visual.general_description: Graphical abstract with a title banner, a three-step text flow with icons on the left, a combined bar and line chart on the right, and a conclusion strip.
visual.detailed_description: A dark blue banner at the top has white text reading "Lemborexant Overdose" and "Presenting with Mild Sedation Despite High Plasma Levels". The left side has three white outlined boxes joined by two downward open arrows. The first box reads "33yo woman ingested", then "Lemborexant 720mg", "Eszopiclone 78mg" and "Alcohol", with icons of a pill bottle with a cross, a blister pack of tablets and a wine glass. The second box reads "4 hours post ingestion (ED arrival)", "GCS 11" and "Plasma Lemborexant : 0.144µg/mL", with an icon of a hospital bed beside an IV pole. The third box reads "9 hours post ingestion", "Full Clinical Recovery (GCS 15)" and "Plasma Lemborexant : 1.410µg/mL", with an icon of a running figure. The right side is a chart with horizontal axis "Time post ingestion (hours)" with ticks 4, 9 and 12. The left vertical axis is "Glasgow Coma Scale" with ticks 10 to 15, next to an orange legend bar. The right vertical axis is "Lemborexant Plasma Concentration (µg/mL)" with ticks 0, 0.5, 1 and 1.5, next to a blue legend bar. A thick orange line rises steadily from the lower left at 4 hours to the upper right at 12 hours. A short blue bar sits at 4 hours and a much taller blue bar at 9 hours; no bar is drawn at 12 hours. A light blue strip at the bottom is headed "Conclusion:" and lists "High Lemborexant levels not always equal severe toxicity", "Supportive Care Effective" and "Massive Lemborexant over dose may not cause life threatening toxicity". No panel letters are visible.

pixel_observations: Title banner reads "Lemborexant Overdose Presenting with Mild Sedation Despite High Plasma Levels".
Left boxes list "33yo woman ingested" lemborexant 720mg, eszopiclone 78mg and alcohol.
Second box prints "GCS 11" and plasma lemborexant 0.144µg/mL at 4 hours post ingestion (ED arrival); third box prints "Full Clinical Recovery (GCS 15)" and 1.410µg/mL at 9 hours post ingestion.
Chart has an orange rising line and blue bars at 4 and 9 hours only.
Bottom strip lists three conclusion statements.

clinical_significance.statement: Authors report that the plasma lemborexant concentration rose from 0.144 µg/mL at four hours to 1.410 µg/mL at nine hours post-ingestion while the patient clinically recovered.

evidence.quote: Retrospective analysis revealed that her plasma lemborexant concentration increased from 0.144 µg/mL at four hours to a peak of 1.410 µg/mL at nine hours post-ingestion, despite undergoing clinical recovery.

limitations: The source has no caption for this graphical abstract; descriptions of its contents come from the pixels.
Fine print is small at the supplied 788 by 443 pixel size; all text above was read in magnified crops.
The orange line does not pass through GCS 15 at the 9 hour tick, so it is not read as plotting the printed GCS 15.
